mainTopic: Bathing in healing waters on שבת, the משנה on medicinal foods and drinks, and the גמרא's identification of those plants with related remedies
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about bathing in healing waters on שבת. The גמרא rejects the idea that the contradicting ברייתות follow a dispute among תנאים about טומאה וטהרה. It then settles on two answers. In the ים הגדול it depends on whether one bathes in the clean water or the polluted water. In מי משרה it depends on whether one lingered in the water. A new משנה then teaches that food healthy people do not eat, like איזוביון, is forbidden on שבת because eating it shows it is medicine. Normal foods and drinks are allowed even for healing. The גמרא identifies the plants in the משנה and explains what each one cures: איזוביון for intestinal worms, יועזר for liver worms, and אבוברואה for גילוי (drinking uncovered liquid). This leads into a long list of folk remedies for liver worms, swallowed venom, a swallowed snake, and a snakebite, with stories showing the cures at work. The last word of the amud begins a new story that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A dispute about purity does not prove a dispute about שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earlier idea that the two ברייתות reflect a dispute among תנאים, because that dispute was only about טומאה וטהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say they argue about purity and impurity, but did you ever hear them argue about שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the previous answer. That answer claimed the two ברייתות about the ים הגדול simply follow two opposing תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא pointed to a dispute over whether the ים הגדול counts like a מקוה for טומאה וטהרה. Here the גמרא says that a dispute in the laws of purity tells us nothing about the laws of שבת. So the contradiction still needs a real answer.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new question. It refutes the answer that came on the previous amud, so the original contradiction is open again.

phrases.english: Say that they disagree regarding impurity and purity,
but regarding Shabbat, did you hear them disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the prior (pre-passage) answer that the contradiction is a dispute among תנאים
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole attempt to explain the contradiction as a dispute among תנאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute was about טומאה וטהרה, not about שבת, so it cannot be carried over to שבת

steps.title: Lingering versus not lingering in the water
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the forbidding ברייתא is about someone who lingered in the water, and the permitting ברייתא is about someone who did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is not difficult. This one is where he stayed in the water; that one is where he did not stay.
steps.whatsHappening: A new answer to the contradiction about the ים הגדול. Staying in the water shows he is bathing for healing, which is forbidden. A quick dip is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer moves the difference from a dispute among תנאים to the facts of the case. Lingering shows a medical purpose, which falls under the ban on רפואה on שבת. A quick dip looks like ordinary bathing or cooling off.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
It is not difficult:
this one is where he lingered,
that one is where he did not linger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer with a new one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות truly contradict, or they reflect a dispute among תנאים
steps.terutzMaskana: The forbidding ברייתא is about lingering (healing); the permitting ברייתא is about a quick dip

steps.title: If he did not linger, even flax water should be allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק: the permitting ברייתא forbids מי משרה, but if it is about not lingering, then מי משרה should be permitted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the last ברייתא? As a case where he did not linger? If he did not linger, then even flax-soaking water should also be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new answer. The permitting ברייתא allowed the ים הגדול but forbade מי משרה. If it is talking about a quick dip, there is no reason to forbid מי משרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule depends only on lingering, then every type of water should follow the same rule. The ברייתא treats the ים הגדול and מי משרה differently, so lingering cannot be what that ברייתא is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you establish (explain the case)?
Water in which flax was soaked

phrases.english: How did you establish the latter one?
Where he did not linger?
If he did not linger,
then even in flax-soaking water it should also be permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of רב נחמן בר יצחק
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the permitting ברייתא is about not lingering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If not lingering is the case, the ברייתא's ban on מי משרה makes no sense, because a quick dip in מי משרה is also permitted

steps.title: A ברייתא shows a quick dip is allowed even in medicinal waters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא proving that without lingering, one may bathe even in מי משרה and other healing waters.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: One may bathe in the waters of Tiberias, in flax water, and in the Sea of Sodom, even if he has sores on his head. When is this said? When he did not linger. But if he lingered, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a source. This ברייתא explicitly allows a quick dip in מי משרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא confirms that a quick dip is allowed even in waters known for healing, and even for someone with wounds on his head. That strengthens the problem from the previous step: a ברייתא about quick dips should not forbid מי משרה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
In what case is this said?

phrases.english: As it was taught:
One may bathe in the waters of Tiberias,
and in flax-soaking water, and in the Sea of Sodom,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ חֲטָטִים בְּרֹאשׁוֹ.
phrases.english: even though he has sores on his head.
In what case is this said?
Where he did not linger;
but if he lingered, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind the challenge
steps.raayaObject: That a quick dip is permitted even in מי משרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing מי טבריא, מי משרה and ימה של סדום

steps.title: The clean part of the sea versus the polluted part
steps.stepSummary: A new answer for the ים הגדול: one ברייתא is about its clean water, where people normally bathe, and the other is about its polluted water, which people enter only for healing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the Great Sea against the Great Sea is not difficult: this is about its good waters, that is about its bad waters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops lingering as the answer for the ים הגדול and gives a different one. It depends on which part of the sea he bathes in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bathing in the clean water looks like normal bathing for pleasure, so it is permitted. Bathing in the polluted water shows a medical purpose, so it is forbidden. Now both ברייתות can be about a quick dip.

phrases.english: Rather, the Great Sea against the Great Sea
is not difficult:
this one is about its good waters,
that one is about its bad waters.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא יָם הַגָּדוֹל אַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after the lingering answer failed for the ים הגדול
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by location within the sea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ים הגדול contradiction is resolved by lingering
steps.terutzMaskana: Clean water is permitted; polluted water (used only for healing) is forbidden

steps.title: The flax-water contradiction is resolved by lingering
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction about מי משרה is answered with the lingering distinction: lingering is forbidden, a quick dip is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Flax water against flax water is also not difficult: this is where he lingered, that is where he did not linger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the second contradiction. For מי משרה, the lingering answer fits well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lingering answer did not work for the ים הגדול, but it does work for מי משרה. Each contradiction ends up with its own answer.
steps.whatToRemember: Final outcome: in the ים הגדול it depends on clean versus polluted water. In מי משרה it depends on lingering versus a quick dip. Anything that shows you are bathing for healing is forbidden on שבת.

phrases.english: Flax water against flax water, also
is not difficult:
this one is where he lingered,
that one is where he did not linger.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵי מִשְׁרָה אַמֵּי מִשְׁרָה נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-part answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מי משרה: a quick dip is permitted, lingering is forbidden; ים הגדול: clean water is permitted, polluted water is forbidden

steps.title: Medicinal-only plants are forbidden; normal ones are allowed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids eating איזוביון on שבת because healthy people do not eat it. It permits יועזר and אבוברואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not eat איזוביון on שבת because it is not food for healthy people. But one may eat יועזר and drink אבוברואה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the basic test: if healthy people do not eat something, eating it on שבת shows it is medicine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is about רפואה on שבת. What matters is how the food looks to others: a food that healthy people do not eat can only be medicine. A food that people normally eat or drink is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A hyssop-type plant used as medicine
A plant (pennyroyal / maidenhair), also eaten normally

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One may not eat eizoveyon on Shabbat
because it is not food of healthy people,
but one may eat yo'ezer,
and drink abuvro'e.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; continues the theme of רפואה on שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food not eaten by healthy people is forbidden on שבת because eating it shows a medical purpose

steps.title: All normal foods and drinks are allowed, except two jaundice remedies
steps.stepSummary: Any food or drink may be taken even for healing, except palm-tree water and כוס עיקרין, which are known remedies for jaundice.
steps.simpleTranslation: All foods a person may eat for healing, and all drinks he may drink, except palm-tree water and a cup of roots, because they are for jaundice.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states the general rule. Normal food stays permitted even when your goal is healing. It then names two drinks as exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because normal food looks like ordinary eating, your private intention to heal does not matter. מי דקלים and כוס עיקרין are known as medicine for jaundice, so drinking them looks like taking medicine.

keyTerms.meaning: A cup of a root-based potion

steps.confusionAlert: The היתר covers eating normal food even with the intent to heal. It is not limited to eating for pleasure.

phrases.english: All foods a person may eat for healing,
and all drinks he may drink,
except palm-tree water and a cup of roots,
because they are for jaundice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the משנה into a general rule with exceptions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Normal foods and drinks are permitted even for healing; מי דקלים and כוס עיקרין are forbidden as jaundice remedies

steps.title: Palm water for thirst and root oil not for healing are allowed
steps.stepSummary: Even the exceptions are permitted when used for a non-medical purpose: palm water to quench thirst and root oil for anointing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one may drink palm-tree water for his thirst, and anoint with root oil not for healing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits its own exceptions. The same items are allowed when they are not used as medicine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban depends on the purpose of the use, not on the item itself. Drinking for thirst or anointing for pleasure is not רפואה, so it is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: Rule of the משנה: what counts is whether the act looks like medicine. Normal foods are always allowed. Medicine-only items are forbidden when used for healing but allowed for ordinary purposes.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שׁוֹתֶה הוּא מֵי דְקָלִים לִצְמָאוֹ,
phrases.english: But one may drink palm-tree water for his thirst,
and anoint with root oil
not for healing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל שׁוֹתֶה הוּא מֵי דְקָלִים לִצְמָאוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the exceptions in the previous step
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Medicinal items are permitted when used for a non-medical purpose

steps.title: רב יוסף names the two kinds of hyssop
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives the local Babylonian names for אזוב and for איזוביון.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יוסף said: אזוב is called 'avarta bar hamag,' and איזוביון is called 'avarta bar hing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה by identifying the plants it mentions. רב יוסף gives the everyday names for the Torah's אזוב and for the איזוביון in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbade איזוביון on שבת, so we first need to know what plant it is. רב יוסף shows that אזוב and איזוביון are two different plants, each with its own local name.

keyTerms.meaning: Hyssop, the plant the Torah uses for purification
A related plant, eaten only as medicine
Local Babylonian plant name (part of both names)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Yosef said:
Hyssop is 'avarta bar hamag,'
eizoveyon is 'avarta bar hing.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's explanation of the plants listed in the משנה (step 7).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אזוב = avarta bar hamag; איזוביון = avarta bar hing.

steps.title: עולא says hyssop is white sage, based on a visit
steps.stepSummary: עולא identifies the Torah's אזוב as white sage, and the גמרא tells the story behind his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: it is white sage. עולא once came to the house of רב שמואל בר יהודה. They brought white sage before him, and he said: 'This is the אזוב written in the Torah.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion: עולא says the Torah's אזוב is white sage. The גמרא supports this with a story where עולא saw white sage and pointed it out as the Torah's אזוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different identification from רב יוסף's. The story shows that עולא's view came from recognizing the actual plant, not just from a name.

keyTerms.meaning: That is written in the Torah

phrases.english: Ulla said:
White sage.
Ulla happened to come
to the house of Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda;
they brought white sage before him.
He said: This is the hyssop
that is written in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different identification of אזוב than רב יוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah's אזוב is white sage.

steps.title: רב פפי says hyssop is shumshuk
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי gives a third identification: the plant called shumshuk.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said: it is shumshuk.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion: רב פפי says the Torah's אזוב is a plant called shumshuk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are three views on what אזוב is. The next step will bring a proof for this one.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant with branches of three stems each (רב פפי's אזוב)

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said:
Shumshuk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third view on the identity of אזוב.

steps.title: A proof for רב פפי from the three stems
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה מדיפתי supports רב פפי: a משנה says the מצוה of אזוב is three branches with three stems each, and shumshuk grows exactly that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה מדיפתי said: רב פפי's view makes sense, because we learned in a משנה: the מצוה of אזוב is three branches, each with three stems, and shumshuk is the plant that is found like that.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה מדיפתי brings proof for רב פפי's view from a משנה about the shape of the אזוב used for the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the אזוב as having three branches, each with three stems. Since shumshuk naturally grows in exactly this pattern, it matches the Torah's אזוב best.

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya of Difti said:
It is reasonable like Rav Pappi,
as we learned: The מצוה of hyssop
is three branches
with three stems on them,
and shumshuk is what is found that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפי's view from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפי's identification of אזוב as shumshuk.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה requiring three branches with three stems each, a shape found in shumshuk.

steps.title: What איזוביון cures and what causes the illness
steps.stepSummary: איזוביון is eaten for intestinal worms, with seven black dates; those worms come from barley flour kept forty days in a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what do people eat it? For intestinal worms. With what do they eat it? With seven black dates. What causes the worms? Barley flour from a vessel that has had it for forty days.
steps.whatsHappening: Back to the איזוביון of our משנה: the גמרא explains what it cures, how to take it, and what causes that illness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows why the משנה forbids איזוביון on שבת: it is purely a medicine for worms, not regular food. The גמרא adds practical medical details as well.
steps.confusionAlert: 'It' here means the איזוביון of the משנה, not the Torah's אזוב that the last few steps were debating.

phrases.english: For what do they eat it? For intestinal worms.
With what do they eat it?
With seven black dates.
From what do they come about?
From barley flour in a vessel
over which forty days have passed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the אזוב debate to the איזוביון of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איזוביון treats intestinal worms, eaten with seven black dates.

steps.title: What is יועזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's permission to eat יועזר and asks what plant it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'But one may eat יועזר.' What is יועזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next plant in the משנה and asks what יועזר is. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed יועזר on שבת, unlike איזוביון. To understand why, we need to know what the plant is.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant the משנה permits eating on שבת

phrases.english: But one may eat yo'ezer.
What is yo'ezer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from איזוביון to the next plant in the משנה.

steps.title: יועזר is potnak
steps.stepSummary: יועזר is the plant called potnak.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is potnak.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: יועזר is the plant known as potnak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives a familiar local name for the plant in the משנה. The next step explains what it is used for.

keyTerms.meaning: Potnak, a plant (often identified as mint)

phrases.english: Potnak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.

steps.title: Potnak cures liver worms, and what causes them
steps.stepSummary: Potnak is eaten for liver worms with seven white dates. Liver worms come from eating certain foods on an empty stomach.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what is it eaten? For liver worms. With what? With seven white dates. What causes them? Raw meat with water on an empty stomach; fatty meat on an empty stomach; ox meat on an empty stomach; nuts on an empty stomach; and fenugreek shoots on an empty stomach, followed by drinking water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what potnak treats (liver worms), how to take it, and lists the foods that cause liver worms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though potnak works as medicine, the משנה allows it on שבת because healthy people also eat it as food. The common thread in the causes is eating heavy foods on an empty stomach.

phrases.english: For what do they eat it? For liver worms.
With what do they eat it?
With seven white dates.
From what do they come about?
From raw meat and water on an empty stomach,
and from fatty meat on an empty stomach,
and from ox meat on an empty stomach,
from nuts on an empty stomach,
and from fenugreek shoots on an empty stomach
and drinking water after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the medical use of the potnak identified in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Potnak treats liver worms, eaten with seven white dates.

steps.title: Backup remedies for liver worms: cress, fasting, meat, vinegar
steps.stepSummary: If potnak is not available or does not help, swallow white cress; if not, fast, suck on a bone of fatty meat roasted on coals, and swallow vinegar.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, he should swallow white cress. And if not, he should sit fasting, bring fatty meat and put it on coals, suck the bone, and swallow vinegar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives backup cures for liver worms in case potnak is missing or does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'ואי לא' means 'and if that does not work or is not available.' The גמרא lists remedies in order, each one a fallback for the one before.

keyTerms.meaning: And if not (if unavailable or ineffective)

phrases.english: And if not,
he should swallow white cress.
And if not, he should sit fasting,
and bring fatty meat
and put it on coals,
and suck the bone,
and swallow vinegar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds fallback remedies for the liver worms of step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fallbacks: white cress; or fasting, sucking a roasted fatty bone, and swallowing vinegar.

steps.title: Some say not to drink vinegar
steps.stepSummary: Some say the vinegar should be left out, because it harms the liver.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: not vinegar, because it is harmful to the liver.
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion removes the vinegar from the previous remedy, because vinegar is bad for the liver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This does not reject the whole remedy, only the vinegar part. The reasoning fits the illness: the problem is in the liver, so something that hurts the liver should be avoided.

phrases.english: And some say: not vinegar,
because it is harmful to the liver.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes one detail (the vinegar) of step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the vinegar part of the remedy.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Vinegar harms the liver, which is the organ being treated.

steps.title: Last resort for liver worms: thorn-bush scrapings in beer
steps.stepSummary: If nothing else works, scrape a thorn bush from top to bottom, boil the scrapings in beer at twilight, drink it the next day with nostrils closed, and relieve himself on a palm trunk.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, bring scrapings of a thorn bush scraped from top to bottom, and not from bottom to top, lest the worms come out through his mouth. Boil it in beer at twilight, and the next day close his nostrils and drink. And when he relieves himself, it should be on the trunk of a palm tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final backup cure for liver worms, with exact instructions for how to prepare and take it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The direction of scraping matters: top to bottom makes the worms leave downward, while bottom to top might make them come up through the mouth. The steps (twilight boiling, closed nostrils, palm trunk) are all part of the folk remedy.

keyTerms.meaning: The trunk of a palm tree

steps.whatToRemember: For liver worms the order is: potnak, then white cress, then fasting with a roasted fatty bone (vinegar disputed), then thorn-bush scrapings boiled in beer.

phrases.english: And if not, let him bring scrapings of a thorn bush
that were scraped from top to bottom,
and not from bottom to top,
lest they come out through his mouth,
and boil it in beer at twilight,
and the next day close his nostrils
and drink it,
and when he relieves himself,
he should relieve himself on the trunk of a palm tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final fallback remedy after those in steps 18-19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Last resort: thorn-bush scrapings (scraped downward) boiled in beer, drunk the next morning with nostrils closed.

steps.title: What is אבוברואה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's permission to drink אבוברואה and asks what it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one may drink אבוברואה.' What is אבוברואה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the last plant in the משנה and asks what אבוברואה is. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה permits drinking אבוברואה on שבת. As with the other plants, the גמרא first identifies it.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant drink the משנה permits on שבת

phrases.english: And one may drink abuvro'e.
What is abuvro'e?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from יועזר to the next plant in the משנה.

steps.title: אבוברואה is the 'lonely staff'
steps.stepSummary: אבוברואה is chumtarya, which means the 'lonely staff.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is chumtarya. What is chumtarya? The lonely staff.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אבוברואה is chumtarya, and then explains that chumtarya means the 'lonely staff.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer is still an unfamiliar name, so the גמרא asks again and explains it further. The name suggests a plant that grows as a single stalk.

keyTerms.meaning: Chumtarya, the plant name for אבוברואה

phrases.english: Chumtarya.
What is chumtarya?
The lonely staff.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21, with a follow-up explanation.

steps.title: The lonely staff treats exposed drinks, with a backup remedy
steps.stepSummary: The lonely staff is used after drinking exposed liquid. If it is unavailable, cook five roses in five cups of beer until a quarter-לוג remains, and drink it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what is it used? For exposed liquids. And if not, bring five roses and five cups of beer, cook them together until it is down to a quarter (of a לוג), and drink it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the lonely staff is a remedy for someone who drank גילוי, liquid left uncovered that a snake may have poisoned. It also gives a backup remedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גילוי is the worry that a snake drank from uncovered liquid and left venom in it. Like the earlier remedies, the backup is introduced with 'ואי לא' for when the main cure is missing or does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Exposed liquid that a snake may have poisoned
A quarter (of a לוג), a liquid measure

steps.whatToRemember: Each plant in the משנה is identified and tied to an illness: איזוביון for intestinal worms, יועזר (potnak) for liver worms, אבוברואה (the lonely staff) for גילוי.

phrases.english: For what do they use it? For exposed liquids.
And if not,
let him bring five roses
and five cups of beer,
and cook them together
until it stands at a quarter-log,
and drink it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the use of the plant identified in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lonely staff treats גילוי; backup: five roses cooked in five cups of beer down to a quarter-לוג.

steps.title: A story of the rose-and-beer cure in action
steps.stepSummary: The mother of רב אחדבוי בר אמי used one rose boiled in one cup of beer, plus a heated oven, to help a man who drank exposed liquid. He vomited out something like a green leaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: The mother of רב אחדבוי בר אמי made a cure for a certain man: one rose and one cup of beer. She boiled them and gave him the drink. She lit the oven, swept out the coals, put a brick inside, and sat him on it. Something like a green leaf came out of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a true story showing the rose-and-beer remedy from the last step working on a real person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 gave a cure of five roses in five cups of beer. Here a smaller version, one rose in one cup, is used, along with heat from an oven. The 'green leaf' that came out is the poison leaving his body, which shows the cure worked.

keyTerms.meaning: A green leaf (here, the vomited poison)

phrases.english: The mother of Rav Aḥadvoi bar Ami
made for a certain man
one rose and one cup of beer.
She boiled it and gave it to him to drink,
and lit the oven and swept out its coals,
(and placed him on a brick)
phrases.notes: An older text version, shown in parentheses. It is replaced by the corrected reading in brackets that follows.

phrases.english: [and placed a brick in it, and sat him] inside it,
phrases.notes: Corrected reading. He sat on the brick so he would not get burned.

phrases.english: and something like a green leaf came out [of him].

steps.triggerLanguage: אִימֵּיהּ דְּרַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי עֲבַדָה לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the rose-and-beer remedy of step 23 being used in a real case.
steps.raayaObject: That boiled rose and beer works against swallowed venom
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story about the mother of רב אחדבוי בר אמי

steps.title: White goat's milk as a cure
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא says a quarter-לוג of milk from a white goat cures swallowed venom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא said: drink a quarter-לוג of milk from a white goat.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds his own remedy for someone who drank exposed liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an argument. It is one more item in a growing list of cures for the same problem. The amount, a quarter-לוג, is a standard small measure.

phrases.english: Rav Avya said:
a quarter-log of milk from a white goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another remedy to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A quarter-לוג of white goat's milk cures swallowed venom.

steps.title: A honey-filled citron roasted on coals
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה says to take a sweet אתרוג, hollow it, fill it with honey, roast it on coals, and eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said: take a sweet אתרוג, make a hole in it, and fill it with honey. Put it on burning coals, then eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: A third remedy for drinking exposed liquid is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This cure is eaten, not drunk, and it needs some preparation: hollowing, filling, and roasting. It is still just another option on the same list.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said:
Let him bring a sweet citron
and hollow it and fill it with honey,
and place it among burning coals, and eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another remedy added to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A honey-filled, roasted sweet אתרוג cures swallowed venom.

steps.title: Aged urine in different amounts for different harms
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says forty-day-old urine helps many problems. The bigger the problem, the bigger the amount: a tiny cup for a hornet sting, a quarter-לוג for a scorpion, half a לוג for exposed liquid, and a full לוג even against כשפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: urine that is forty days old works like this. A tiny cupful helps a hornet sting. A quarter-לוג helps a scorpion bite. Half a לוג helps someone who drank exposed liquid. A full לוג helps even against כשפים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives one remedy with a sliding scale. The dose goes up as the danger goes up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is a ranking of dangers. A hornet is the mildest, then a scorpion, then exposed liquid, and כשפים is the most serious. Exposed liquid sits third, which shows how seriously חז"ל took it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said,
urine that is forty days old:
a very small cupful, for a hornet sting;
a quarter-log, for a scorpion bite;
half a log, for exposed liquid;
a log is effective even against witchcraft.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר, מֵי רַגְלַיִם בְּנֵי אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the list. One remedy is given for several dangers, including exposed liquid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forty-day-old urine, in rising amounts, treats a hornet sting, a scorpion bite, exposed liquid, and כשפים.

steps.title: Herb waters and balsam help against both dangers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says spinach water, avangar water, and balsam work both for exposed liquid and against כשפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: anigron (water from boiled spinach), avangar (water from a boiled grass), and balsam help both against exposed liquid and against כשפים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן ends this run of remedies with three items that work for two different dangers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא needed a bigger dose for כשפים than for exposed liquid. רבי יוחנן's three items cover both dangers without that distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: Water in which spinach (or beets) was boiled
Water in which a certain grass was boiled

steps.whatToRemember: The list of cures for exposed liquid is now done: rose-and-beer, white goat's milk, a honey-filled אתרוג, aged urine, and herb waters or balsam.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
spinach water, and avangar water, and balsam
are effective both for exposed liquid and for witchcraft.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the list of remedies with items that work for both exposed liquid and כשפים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anigron, avangar, and balsam help both against exposed liquid and against כשפים.

steps.title: Cure for someone who swallowed a snake
steps.stepSummary: A person who swallowed a snake should eat hops with salt and then run three מילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone swallowed a snake, feed him hops with salt and make him run three מילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new danger: a person who swallowed a whole snake, not just its poison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic. The cure has two parts: something to eat, and hard running. The running is meant to shake the snake loose so it leaves the body.

keyTerms.meaning: מילין, units of distance (about a kilometer each)

phrases.english: One who swallowed a snake
should be fed hops with salt,
and be made to run three mil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from swallowed venom to a swallowed snake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hops with salt, followed by running three מילין, removes a swallowed snake.

steps.title: רב שימי בר אשי uses the snake cure
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי saw a man who swallowed a snake. Disguised as a horseman, he fed him hops with salt and made him run three מילין, and the snake came out in pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי saw a man who had swallowed a snake. He made himself look like a horseman. He fed the man hops with salt and made him run ahead of him for three מילין, and the snake came out of him in pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: A story shows the snake cure from the last step working.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The horseman disguise explains how a sick man could be made to run three מילין. He was chased by a rider, which scared him into running. The snake coming out in pieces shows the cure worked.

keyTerms.meaning: He appeared to him as / disguised himself

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi saw
a certain man who had swallowed a snake.
He appeared to him as a horseman.
He fed him hops with salt
and made him run before him three mil,
and it came out of him in pieces.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי חַזְיֵיהּ לְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing the cure from step 29.
steps.raayaObject: That hops with salt and running removes a swallowed snake
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story of רב שימי בר אשי

steps.title: Another version: אליהו cures רב שימי בר אשי
steps.stepSummary: Some say רב שימי בר אשי himself swallowed the snake. אליהו הנביא came disguised as a horseman and gave him the same cure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it was רב שימי בר אשי who swallowed a snake. אליהו came and appeared to him as a horseman. He fed him hops with salt and made him run ahead of him three מילין, and the snake came out of him in pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way the same story is told. Only the roles change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רב שימי is the patient, and אליהו is the healer on horseback. The cure itself is exactly the same, so the proof for the cure stays the same either way.
steps.confusionAlert: The cure is the same in both versions. The only difference is who swallowed the snake and who healed him.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי בְּלַע חִיוְיָא,
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi swallowed a snake,
Elijah came and appeared to him as a horseman.
He fed him hops with salt
and made him run before him three mil
and it came out of him in pieces.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי בְּלַע חִיוְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of the same story.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A version in which אליהו heals רב שימי בר אשי

steps.title: Cure for a snakebite
steps.stepSummary: For a snakebite, tear open the fetus of a white donkey and place it on the bite.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a snake bit someone, bring the fetus of a white donkey, tear it open, and place it on the bite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from swallowing a snake to being bitten by one, and gives a cure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This cure goes on the outside of the body, on the wound itself. It is not eaten or drunk. It is a new case within the snake topic.

phrases.english: One who was bitten by a snake
should bring the fetus of a white donkey,
tear it open, and place it on the bite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a swallowed snake to a snakebite.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A torn-open white donkey fetus placed on the wound treats a snakebite.

steps.title: A limit on the donkey cure
steps.stepSummary: The donkey-fetus cure works only if the animal is not a טרפה. This passage then ends with the first word of a new story.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only when it is not found to be a טרפה. A certain...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a condition to the snakebite cure. The final word 'הָהוּא' begins the next story and sets up what comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cure is limited: an animal with a fatal defect (טרפה) does not work. The cure stays the same, but now it only applies in certain cases.

keyTerms.meaning: And this applies only (introduces a limit)
An animal with a defect that will cause it to die

steps.confusionAlert: The last word 'הָהוּא' is not part of this rule. It is the opening of the next story.

phrases.english: And this applies only when it is not found to be a tereifa.
A certain...
phrases.notes: Opening word of the next story, which continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the snakebite cure in step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The donkey-fetus cure works only when the animal is not a טרפה.
